name: Desktop engine login service
summary: The desktop app can run the engine as a headless login service that starts at login with no window, restarts itself on an update and hands every Dock click to a real window; it is built and switchable but off by default (the detached engine stays the default).
where: Settings, desktop app, the three login rows (start the engine at login, open carnivore in the background at login, open a window at login), when the engine host is set to launchd-agent.
System Settings, General, Login Items and Extensions, the Carnivore row.
how_to: Set CARNIVORE_ENGINE_HOST=launchd-agent, or write {"strategy": "launchd-agent"} to engine-host.json in the app's data folder, then open the app: the engine login service is registered and starts at login with no Dock icon and no window.
Click the Dock icon while only the service runs: a real window opens and adopts the running engine.

Uninstall Carnivore (the tray, or uninstall.sh) or run nuke.sh: the app unregisters the engine login service, both LaunchAgent labels go, your privacy rows are reset and your projects stay; terminal sessions keep running unless you add --stop-tmux.
examples: Reboot the computer: the engine is healthy again 30 seconds after login with no window and your tmux sessions untouched.
Install a new version over the old one: the service restarts itself onto the new bundle and the new version serves, sessions unchanged.
After uninstall, launchctl print shows no ai.carnivore.menubar job and ~/carnivore-projects is untouched.
media_exempt: headless login service, nothing to screenshot
